name: The Cerise Recoil

detectability.signature: Pink-white annihilation flashes at erratic intervals; gamma bloom detectable across half a sector.

proximity: Gamma counters climb steadily as annihilation vapors diffuse outward
Magnetometers twitch toward the pocket as if it were a magnet for matter
contact: Any matter crossing the boundary annihilates in a flash of cerise light
Shockwaves from interior annihilations batter hulls at random intervals
prolonged_exposure: Cumulative radiation dose proves lethal to exposed crews within hours
Vessels lingering too close are dismantled flash by flash, atom by opposed atom

phenomena: Antimatter annihilation flashes in shades of pink and white
Exotic particles detectable on sensors — antiproton streams off the boundary
Matter spontaneously changing state within the contamination shell around it
hazards: Complete ship destruction upon boundary contact
Molecular disintegration of exposed crew and equipment
Radiation exposure exceeding safe limits across the entire approach cone
opportunities: Exotic matter collection — the densest natural antihydrogen reserve ever surveyed
Energy harvesting potential limited only by courage and containment engineering
Data valuable to scientific institutions studying baryon asymmetry
known_incidents: The freighter Halcyon Step clipped the contamination shell in 2320; the resulting flash was mistaken for a supernova on three separate charts.
Automated harvester barges now skim the outer boundary, returning antihydrogen worth more than their own weight in warship hulls — when they return.
description: The Cerise Recoil is a sphere of seething negation barely twenty-six kilometers wide, wrapped in a contamination haze of pink-white flashes. It orbits a burnt-out companion no chart has bothered to name, a jewel set on a dead hand. Gamma telescopes across the sector tick in its direction like nervous clocks.

Matter that touches the boundary simply stops being, converting itself into light with theatrical efficiency. Interior annihilations fire at no interval any statistician has tamed, hurling shockwaves through the surrounding vacuum. The pocket circles its dark companion in a chaotic waltz, its boundary breathing — sometimes generously, sometimes not.

Surveys date the pocket to a baryon-violating event 2.1 billion years past, a leftover lump of the universe's missing antiside. In 2320 the freighter Halcyon Step grazed the contamination shell; three separate observatories logged the flash as a supernova. The subsequent lawsuit established, for legal purposes, that a region of space can be considered an unsafe workplace.

Automated barges now skim its outer reaches for antihydrogen, fueling the most expensive engines ever lit. Insurance consortia post standing rewards for a predictive model of its flashes; the reward grows yearly, unclaimed. Captains crossing the approach cone are advised to be fast, quiet, and philosophically prepared.
